evaluation_inputs.system_description: An Event framework where the application logic and framework are highly inter-dependent. The Main module is part of the framework, and the Event Manager interacts directly with application handlers. It features an Event Queue and a base Handler component extended by standard and application-specific handlers.

phase_1_discovery.initial_documentation_status: Fully developed architecture with class diagrams, component descriptions, and defined component interactions.
evaluator_inquiry_questions: Can the components of the architecture be reused for future projects?
Can the framework be expanded in the future to accommodate a new application or new components?
Will the system handle any input given by the user and handle invalid input?
Is the architecture consistent in behavior?
Can any new application-specific functionality be added to the architecture?
Can the system be modified in short time and cost-effective manner?
Does the architecture perform its event-processing task properly?

architectural_approaches.approach_name: Event-driven framework with event queue and FIFO dispatch
architectural_approaches.description: The supplied architecture describes an Event framework in which an Event Queue is used and runtime constraints require events to be dispatched in a First-Come-First-Served (FIFO) pattern. The system maintains an idle wait state until input is received.

addressed_attributes.rationale: FIFO event queuing and sequential event processing are the only explicitly supplied mechanisms relevant to event handling speed, but the inputs also state the transaction speed is qualitative and slow due to a high number of components involved.
The queue-based dispatch and idle-wait behavior indicate controlled event handling, though no explicit fault-handling mechanism is supplied beyond a STOP handler constraint.
Event dispatching through the framework is central to the business goals and system description.

architectural_approaches.description: The system description states that application logic and framework are highly inter-dependent, the Main module is part of the framework, and the Event Manager interacts directly with application handlers. The architecture therefore couples framework services closely to application-specific handlers.

addressed_attributes.rationale: Direct interaction between the Event Manager and application handlers enables event processing and application-specific behavior.
The high inter-dependence of application logic and framework components suggests modification is possible but likely tightly constrained by the coupling described in the inputs.
The presence of standard and application-specific handlers indicates some variation points, but the extent is not specified.

architectural_approaches.approach_name: Handler hierarchy with base handler extended by standard and application-specific handlers
architectural_approaches.description: The system includes a base Handler component that is extended by standard and application-specific handlers, indicating an inheritance-based extension mechanism within the framework.

addressed_attributes.rationale: Extending a base Handler supports addition of application-specific functionality, consistent with the business goal of allowing application components to utilize framework services.
The base/extended handler structure supports variation in handler behavior.
Handler specialization supports processing different event or application behaviors.
